pre_registered_claim.C: Voluntary force loss during fatigue has a genuine CENTRAL (CNS-level) component distinct from peripheral/muscular failure, quantified by the interpolated-twitch technique (voluntary activation, VA%, falls with fatigue from a real, reproducible, subject-specific baseline). This central component includes a genuine supraspinal/cortical contribution (dissociable from spinal and peripheral changes via TMS + ischaemia). Group III/IV muscle afferents ACTIVELY REGULATE central motor drive as a protective governor -- pharmacological blockade increases central drive AND increases peripheral fatigue on a decorrelated (muscle-biopsy metabolite) measurement axis, and the naive 'it just disinhibits effort' adversary gets the sign of the overall-performance effect wrong. Central:peripheral apportionment is task-dependent, not a fixed ratio. Chronic fatigue syndrome shows a disproportionate, axis-orthogonal central-only deficit; multiple sclerosis shows a genuinely MIXED central+peripheral deficit; overtraining syndrome's central-fatigue link is a real but currently OPEN gap in the primary literature.
pre_registered_claim.not_C: (a) The measured 'VA decline' is noise, submaximal motivation, or antagonist co-contraction, not a real reproducible central signal. (b) Any TMS/cortical-stimulation-revealed 'central' signal is actually a peripheral muscle-property artifact (e.g. potentiation/depression) riding along with fatigue, not a genuine upstream (CNS) phenomenon. (c) Group III/IV afferent feedback has no real causal/regulatory role in central drive or peripheral-fatigue severity -- pharmacological blockade effects are a generic sedative/disinhibition artifact of the drug, not true afferent-signal removal, and/or blockade should straightforwardly IMPROVE performance if the 'brake' story were right. (d) A single, fixed central:peripheral ratio applies across all tasks/muscle groups. (e) CFS/MS central-fatigue findings are fully explained by generalized deconditioning/peripheral myopathy, not a genuine CNS-specific deficit.
pre_registered_claim.threshold_preregistered: F1: >=1 independent reliability study (between-subject consistency, ruled-out antagonist-coactivation confound) PLUS >=2 independent fatigue studies showing a significant VA decline of >=5 percentage points from a >=95% baseline -- else not_C(a) stands. F2: a TMS-specific superimposed-twitch increment must grow with fatigue AND fail to recover under an ischaemia block that a decorrelated cortical-excitability signal, recorded in the SAME ischaemia, DOES recover from (a forced double dissociation) -- else not_C(b) stands. F3: pharmacological group III/IV afferent blockade (with a resting-cardioventilatory control ruling out a generic drug effect) must INCREASE central drive (EMG/iEMG) AND INCREASE peripheral fatigue (twitch-force decline) across >=2 independent protocols, confirmed on a decorrelated non-EMG/force leg (muscle-biopsy metabolite chemistry) that itself correlates with the twitch deficit -- else not_C(c) stands; additionally the sign of the OVERALL PERFORMANCE effect must be checked, not assumed. F4: >=2 decorrelated modalities/muscle groups must show materially different central:peripheral apportionment -- else not_C(d) stands. F5: VA must be significantly lower in CFS patients vs controls WHILE peripheral markers (metabolism, M-wave, twitch tension) are statistically indistinguishable -- else not_C(e, CFS half) stands. F6: the 'MS fatigue is purely central' adversary must be tested against a voluntary-drive-BYPASSING protocol (electrical stimulation) -- if that protocol still shows excess MS fatigue, not_C(e, MS half) as a PURE-peripheral-explanation-only claim is refuted, but a pure-central claim is ALSO refuted, forcing a mixed verdict.
pre_registered_claim.adversary_forced: (a) forced via Allen/Gandevia/McKenzie 1995's own reliability design (5 subjects x 5 days x 10 MVCs, antagonist-coactivation explicitly checked and ruled out). (b) forced via Gandevia et al 1996's own built-in ischaemia control (voluntary force/VA does not recover in ischaemia; TMS-EMG excitability changes DO recover in the identical ischaemia) and independently via McNeil et al 2009's spinal-level time-course dissociation (30s vs 90s recovery) using a DIFFERENT technique (cervicomedullary stimulation vs TMS-conditioning). (c) forced via Amann et al 2011's own explicit resting-cardioventilatory-unchanged control, AND via checking the SIGN of the overall performance effect (time-to-exhaustion got SHORTER, not longer, under blockade -- the opposite of what a naive disinhibition story predicts), AND via Blain et al 2016's decorrelated muscle-biopsy metabolite leg (a completely different instrument/observable than EMG or twitch force). (d) forced via Millet & Lepers 2004's explicit within-and-between-modality task-dependency findings and Enoka & Duchateau 2008's explicit rejection of a 'global mechanism'. (e) forced via Sharma et al 1995's own electrically-stimulated (central-bypassing) protocol in MS, which STILL shows excess fatigue -- refuting a pure-peripheral-only account of the twitch-occlusion finding would be wrong too, but so is a pure-central account; the forced adversary survives PARTIALLY, yielding an honest MIXED verdict rather than a clean win for either C or not_C on MS specifically.

falsifier_tests.measure: twitch-interpolation reliability study (fresh, non-fatigued subjects) + independent fatigue-protocol VA decline in >=2 muscle groups/techniques

evidence.cite: Gandevia SC. Spinal and supraspinal factors in human muscle fatigue. Physiol Rev. 2001;81(4):1725-89.
evidence.value: Direct quote: 'Much data suggest that voluntary activation of human motoneurons and muscle fibers is suboptimal and thus maximal voluntary force is commonly less than true maximal force... Voluntary activation usually diminishes during maximal voluntary isometric tasks, that is central fatigue develops, and motor unit firing rates decline.' Reviews twitch interpolation as the revealing technique and names group III/IV muscle afferents as a spinal-level contributor.
evidence.role: overarching review anchor for the whole F1 claim, not a single-experiment data point

evidence.cite: Belanger AY, McComas AJ. Extent of motor unit activation during effort. J Appl Physiol Respir Environ Exerc Physiol. 1981;51(5):1131-5.
evidence.value: Bibliographic record confirmed live (title/journal/volume/pages/DOI); no abstract text retrievable via efetch this session (short-form/pre-modern-abstract record). Cited for provenance as one of the classic papers establishing quantitative motor-unit-activation measurement during voluntary effort, not for a specific extracted number this session.
evidence.role: methodological provenance, honest gap on abstract content disclosed

evidence.cite: Allen GM, Gandevia SC, McKenzie DK. Reliability of measurements of muscle strength and voluntary activation using twitch interpolation. Muscle Nerve. 1995;18(6):593-600.
evidence.n: 5 subjects x 5 days x 10 MVCs, elbow flexors
evidence.value: Subjects did not drive the stimulated elbow flexors maximally in 75% of ALL contractions, even fresh/non-fatigued -- VA<100% is a common, real, reproducible baseline trait. Consistent between-subject differences (P<0.01); no significant within-subject difference across days in 4/5 subjects; explicitly NOT associated with antagonist co-contraction.

evidence.cite: Gandevia SC, Allen GM, Butler JE, Taylor JL. Supraspinal factors in human muscle fatigue: evidence for suboptimal output from the motor cortex. J Physiol. 1996;490(Pt2):529-36.
evidence.n: human subjects, biceps brachii, sustained MVC
evidence.value: Voluntary activation of biceps fell from an average of >99% to an average of 90.7% over a 3-min sustained MVC.

evidence.cite: Bigland-Ritchie B, Jones DA, Hosking GP, Edwards RH. Central and peripheral fatigue in sustained maximum voluntary contractions of human quadriceps muscle. Clin Sci Mol Med. 1978;54(6):609-14.
evidence.value: In 6/9 subjects, voluntary force fell faster than tetanic-stimulation force with EMG amplitude falling in parallel (central fatigue present); those subjects could transiently boost force AND EMG together with an extra effort, demonstrating real unused reserve. In 3/9, force declined in parallel with tetanic reference and EMG stayed constant while force fell ~60% (little/no central fatigue in this subgroup).

falsifier_tests.note: The reliability study and the fatigue studies are DECORRELATED in design (one tests reproducibility in non-fatigued subjects; the others measure change with a fatiguing protocol in different muscle groups/techniques -- biceps via twitch interpolation, quadriceps via tetanic-stimulation comparison) yet converge: VA is a real, subject-specific, reproducible quantity that measurably falls with fatigue, not an artifact of measurement noise or motivation.

falsifier_tests.measure: TMS-evoked superimposed-twitch increment during fatigue + built-in post-fatigue ischaemia double-dissociation control; independent spinal-level time-course replication

evidence.cite: Gandevia SC, Allen GM, Butler JE, Taylor JL. Supraspinal factors in human muscle fatigue: evidence for suboptimal output from the motor cortex. J Physiol. 1996;490(Pt2):529-36.
evidence.value: TMS-evoked force increment (relative to voluntary force) rose from 1.0% (fresh) to 9.8% (after a 2-min MVC) -- cortical output was not maximal at the time of stimulation. Post-fatigue ischaemia (sphygmomanometer cuff) did NOT restore voluntary force or VA, but fatigue-induced changes in EMG responses to magnetic cortical stimulation RECOVERED RAPIDLY despite maintained ischaemia -- a forced double dissociation: a single shared peripheral confound cannot produce opposite recovery behaviour in two signals under the identical block.

evidence.cite: McNeil CJ, Martin PG, Gandevia SC, Taylor JL. The response to paired motor cortical stimuli is abolished at a spinal level during human muscle fatigue. J Physiol. 2009;587(Pt23):5601-12.
evidence.value: Paired-pulse TMS (long-interval intracortical inhibition, 100ms conditioning-test interval) vs cervicomedullary stimulation (bypasses the cortex, directly activates corticospinal tract): both conditioned MEPs AND CMEPs collapsed within 30s of a 2-min MVC (spinal, not purely cortical, contribution). Unconditioned MEP/CMEP responses recovered in <30s; conditioned MEPs/CMEPs required 90s -- an independent, differently-derived time-course dissociation (a second forced double-dissociation using a different technique).

evidence.cite: Taylor JL, Todd G, Gandevia SC. Evidence for a supraspinal contribution to human muscle fatigue. Clin Exp Pharmacol Physiol. 2006;33(4):400-5.
evidence.value: Supraspinal fatigue accounts for 'about one-quarter of the loss of force' during fatiguing sustained/intermittent elbow-flexor contractions -- a specific, muscle-group-scoped quantitative anchor, not claimed as a universal figure.

falsifier_tests.note: Two independently-derived double dissociations (an ischaemia-vs-TMS-EMG dissociation in #8821149; a time-course-of-recovery dissociation between conditioned and unconditioned responses in #19805743, using a genuinely different stimulation technique) both rule out a shared-peripheral-confound explanation for the observed 'central' signal.

falsifier_tests.measure: invariant-ceiling signature across different pre-fatigue trajectories (regulator test) + pharmacological (fentanyl) group III/IV afferent blockade vs placebo, central drive (EMG/iEMG) and peripheral fatigue (twitch force + decorrelated muscle-biopsy metabolite chemistry), across 3 independent protocols, with an explicit control ruling out a generic drug effect and a sign-check on overall performance

evidence.cite: Amann M, Dempsey JA. Locomotor muscle fatigue modifies central motor drive in healthy humans and imposes a limitation to exercise performance. J Physiol. 2008;586(1):161-73.
evidence.value: Two different pre-fatigue protocols (83% vs 67% peak power output) before an identical 5km time trial: central motor drive (quadriceps EMG) fell -23% with the higher pre-fatigue dose vs control, but end-exercise peripheral quadriceps-twitch decline (DeltaQtw,pot) converged to the SAME -35% to -37% regardless of pre-fatigue level (P=0.35, no significant difference) -- the invariant-ceiling signature of a real regulator (different trajectories, same endpoint).

evidence.cite: Amann M, Proctor LT, Sebranek JJ, Pegelow DF, Dempsey JA. Opioid-mediated muscle afferents inhibit central motor drive and limit peripheral muscle fatigue development in humans. J Physiol. 2009;587(1):271-83.
evidence.value: Double-blind, placebo-controlled, 5km cycling TT: lumbar intrathecal fentanyl (L3-L4) vs placebo. iEMG (central drive) +12+/-3% in first half (P<0.05); DeltaQtw -46+/-2% (fentanyl) vs -33+/-2% (placebo), P<0.001. Blood lactate 16.3+/-0.5 vs 12.6+/-1.0%; arterial O2 saturation 89+/-1 vs 94+/-1%. Fentanyl had NO effect on resting quadriceps strength (rules out a direct muscle-level drug effect).

evidence.cite: Amann M, Blain GM, Proctor LT, Sebranek JJ, Pegelow DF, Dempsey JA. Implications of group III and IV muscle afferents for high-intensity endurance exercise performance in humans. J Physiol. 2011;589(Pt21):5299-309.
evidence.value: Constant-load cycling (80% Wpeak) to exhaustion, fentanyl vs placebo. Explicit control: 'unchanged resting cardioventilatory responses' (rules out a generic sedative confound). CMD +9+/-3% at end-exercise (P<0.05). Time to exhaustion SHORTER with fentanyl (6.8+/-0.3 vs 8.7+/-0.3 min). End-exercise DeltaQtw,pot about one-third greater (-44+/-2% vs -34+/-2%); rate of peripheral fatigue development 67+/-10% greater (P<0.01). Ventilatory/circulatory cost of blockade documented: 9% lower VE/VCO2, 5 mmHg higher end-tidal PCO2, 3% lower Hb saturation, 8-10% lower arterial pressure/heart rate.

evidence.cite: Blain GM, Mangum TS, Sidhu SK, Weavil JC, Hureau TJ, Jessop JE, Bledsoe AD, Richardson RS, Amann M. Group III/IV muscle afferents limit the intramuscular metabolic perturbation during whole body exercise in humans. J Physiol. 2016;594(18):5303-15.
evidence.value: 5km TT with vastus lateralis muscle biopsies pre/post (a DECORRELATED measurement axis -- mass-spectrometry intramuscular metabolite chemistry, not EMG or force). Motoneuronal output (EMG) +21+/-12% with fentanyl (P<0.05). Intramuscular Pi +55%, H+ +62%, ADP +129%, lactate +47% (all P<0.001), PCr depletion +27% (P<0.01) greater with fentanyl. DeltaQTsingle -52+/-2% (fentanyl) vs -31+/-1% (control), correlated with DeltaPi (r^2=0.79, P<0.01) and DeltaH+ (r^2=0.92, P<0.01). Time to complete the FIXED-DISTANCE TT was similar (~8.8 min both conditions) -- a disclosed, genuine protocol-dependent contrast with the fixed-workload-to-exhaustion design (PMID 21878520) where time-to-exhaustion WAS shortened.

falsifier_tests.note: The forced adversary ('fentanyl effect is generic disinhibition/sedation, not true afferent-signal removal') is defeated two ways: (1) resting cardioventilatory responses were explicitly documented unchanged, so the effect only manifests during exercise when the blocked afferents would be active; (2) the SIGN of the overall performance effect is wrong for a naive disinhibition story -- time-to-exhaustion got SHORTER under blockade, not longer, because the same afferents that cap central drive also support adequate ventilation/circulation during exercise. The three replications span 2 different task structures (fixed-distance TT, fixed-workload-to-exhaustion) and one completely different measurement instrument (muscle biopsy mass spectrometry vs surface EMG/electrically-evoked twitch force), all converging on the same direction.

evidence.cite: Millet GY, Lepers R. Alterations of neuromuscular function after prolonged running, cycling and skiing exercises. Sports Med. 2004;34(2):105-16.
evidence.value: Names 'task dependency of muscle fatigue' as the organizing principle. Central fatigue after prolonged running is measurable via twitch interpolation, EMG/M-wave ratio, or voluntary-vs-evoked force comparison; central activation deficit is ATTENUATED in activities inducing less muscle damage (e.g. cycling) at matched duration. After a 30km run, individuals with the greatest knee-extensor strength loss showed the largest activation deficit specifically (a within-modality dose relationship).

evidence.cite: Taylor JL, Gandevia SC. A comparison of central aspects of fatigue in submaximal and maximal voluntary contractions. J Appl Physiol. 2008;104(2):542-50.
evidence.value: Central fatigue is demonstrable even in brief maximal efforts nested inside a weak (<15% max) ongoing contraction; group III/IV afferent activity acts supraspinally to limit motor cortical output. Best submaximal-task signature: disproportionate rise in perceived effort relative to force output -- a distinct observable from maximal-contraction VA decline.

evidence.cite: Enoka RM, Duchateau J. Muscle fatigue: what, why and how it influences muscle function. J Physiol. 2008;586(1):11-23.
evidence.value: Direct quote: 'there is no global mechanism responsible for muscle fatigue... the mechanisms that cause fatigue are specific to the task being performed.'

falsifier_tests.note: The ~25% supraspinal-fatigue figure (F2, PMID 16620309) is explicitly scoped to sustained elbow-flexor MVCs; this falsifier test confirms that figure should NOT be extrapolated as a universal constant across muscle groups/modalities -- running, cycling, skiing, and submaximal-vs-maximal contractions all show materially different apportionment.

falsifier_tests.measure: twitch-interpolation VA + parallel peripheral markers (metabolic response, M-wave amplitude, twitch tension) in CFS patients vs matched controls

evidence.cite: Kent-Braun JA, Sharma KR, Weiner MW, Massie B, Miller RG. Central basis of muscle fatigue in chronic fatigue syndrome. Neurology. 1993;43(1):125-31.
evidence.n: CFS patients vs controls, tibialis anterior, intermittent submaximal + sustained maximal isometric protocols
evidence.value: Direct quote: 'The extent of fatigue, metabolic response, and changes in both M-wave amplitude and twitch tension during exercise were similar in patients and controls. The response to systemic exercise was also normal in the patients. However, voluntary activation of the tibialis was significantly lower in the patients during maximal sustained exercise... This failure of activation was well in excess of that found in controls, suggesting an important central component of muscle fatigue in CFS.'

falsifier_tests.note: A clean orthogonal-axis result: the entire peripheral coordinate (metabolism, M-wave, twitch tension, systemic exercise response) is statistically unchanged; only the central coordinate (VA) is shifted. This is the pattern a genuine CNS-specific deficit predicts and a generalized-deconditioning/peripheral-myopathy account of CFS fatigue does not.

falsifier_tests.verdict: PASS_AS_MIXED (forced, disclosed, not swept aside -- the pure-central adversary does not fully fall, and neither does a pure-peripheral one)
falsifier_tests.measure: twitch-occlusion VA (voluntary-drive-dependent) vs electrically-stimulated (voluntary-drive-bypassing) fatigability, in MS patients vs controls

evidence.cite: Rice CL, Vollmer TL, Bigland-Ritchie B. Neuromuscular responses of patients with multiple sclerosis. Muscle Nerve. 1992;15(10):1123-32.
evidence.value: Twitch occlusion: normal subjects could activate their muscles maximally; MS patients 'rarely achieved greater than 60% activation.' Motoneuron firing rates in MS rarely exceeded 17 Hz vs ~24 Hz in normals.

evidence.cite: Kent-Braun JA, Sharma KR, Weiner MW, Miller RG. Effects of exercise on muscle activation and metabolism in multiple sclerosis. Muscle Nerve. 1994;17(10):1162-9.
evidence.value: MVC fell sooner in MS but similarly overall by end of exercise. End-exercise Pi/PCr: 1.86+/-0.22 (controls) vs 0.66+/-0.04 (MS), P<0.01. pH: 6.75+/-0.04 (controls, fell) vs 7.06+/-0.04 (MS, unchanged), P<0.01 -- a smaller metabolic perturbation at matched relative intensity, consistent with incomplete muscle engagement even in MILD MS.

evidence.cite: Sharma KR, Kent-Braun J, Mynhier MA, Weiner MW, Miller RG. Evidence of an abnormal intramuscular component of fatigue in multiple sclerosis. Muscle Nerve. 1995;18(12):1403-11.
evidence.value: 9 minutes of intermittent ELECTRICAL STIMULATION, explicitly 'used to eliminate central sources of muscle fatigue' (voluntary drive bypassed by construction): decline in tetanic force, phosphocreatine, and intracellular pH was GREATER in MS patients than controls. CMAP amplitude did not decrease (rules out neuromuscular-junction failure). Tetanic-force recovery was delayed post-exercise in patients (suggests abnormal excitation-contraction coupling). Authors' own conclusion, quoted: fatigue in MS has 'both central (perception, upper motor neuron dysfunction) and peripheral (impaired metabolism and excitation-contraction coupling) components.'

falsifier_tests.note: The 'MS fatigue is purely central/UMN' adversary is forced onto its hardest test -- a protocol that bypasses voluntary drive entirely -- and FAILS to fully explain the excess MS fatigue found there, forcing a genuinely mixed verdict. This is the sharpest possible symmetric-QC test available in the located literature: MS shows the LARGEST central (twitch-occlusion) deficit of any condition surveyed in this document (~60% ceiling vs ~100% normal) while simultaneously proving a real peripheral component exists via a design that removes the central axis by construction.

falsifier_tests.verdict: OPEN (honest gap, forced once via OODA before declaring, not a zero-effort honest-negative)
falsifier_tests.measure: targeted search for a direct twitch-interpolation/voluntary-activation study in diagnosed overtraining syndrome (2 title-restricted search angles: 'overtraining'+voluntary-activation, 'overreaching'+'central fatigue')

evidence.cite: Meeusen R, Duclos M, Foster C, Fry A, Gleeson M, Nieman D, Raglin J, Rietjens G, Steinacker J, Urhausen A; European College of Sport Science; American College of Sports Medicine. Prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of the overtraining syndrome: joint consensus statement. Med Sci Sports Exerc. 2013;45(1):186-205.
evidence.value: Direct quote: of the several markers currently used (hormonal, performance, psychological, biochemical/immune), 'none of them meet all the criteria to make their use generally accepted.' No twitch-interpolation/VA-specific criterion is named anywhere in the consensus statement.

evidence.cite: Aubry A, Hausswirth C, Louis J, Coutts AJ, Buchheit M, Le Meur Y. The Development of Functional Overreaching Is Associated with a Faster Heart Rate Recovery in Endurance Athletes. PLoS One. 2015;10(10):e0139754.
evidence.value: 10/21 overload-group triathletes developed functional overreaching (f-OR); this subgroup showed faster heart-rate recovery during the overload period, which the authors interpret as potentially reflecting a 'decreased central command and... lower chemoreflex activity.' An autonomic/cardiovascular-axis finding, NOT a voluntary-muscle-force or twitch-interpolation measurement.

falsifier_tests.note: Genuinely searched for and not found this session; the field's own 2013 consensus statement confirms this is not merely a one-session search failure but an actual, currently open gap in the primary literature. Reported as OPEN rather than forced into a false PASS by stretching the Aubry 2015 autonomic finding to cover the same construct as F1-F6's voluntary-activation/twitch-interpolation measurements.

geometric_mechanism.twitch_interpolation_as_null_space_proje: The achievable force of a muscle at an instant is a point on a manifold set by which motor units are recruited and at what firing rate (the recruitment-threshold/rate-coding geometry docs/MECHANISM_MOTOR_UNIT.md builds explicitly for soleus). A supramaximal electrical shock delivered during a voluntary effort can only add force by exciting whatever capacity voluntary drive left UNUSED -- unrecruited motor units, or units firing below fusion. If voluntary drive already occupies the full achievable manifold (VA=100%), the shock has nothing orthogonal to add and the superimposed twitch is exactly zero; if drive is submaximal, the shock's evoked increment is a direct, quantitative readout of the unused (null-space) dimension of the recruitment/rate-coding space. VA% = [1 - (superimposed twitch / potentiated resting twitch)] x 100 is the field-standard formula built on exactly this logic (used throughout the cited twitch-interpolation literature; NOT independently re-derived from a live-quoted primary-source formula this session -- disclosed honest gap).
geometric_mechanism.group_III_IV_feedback_as_a_measured_regu: Treating (central motor drive, accumulated peripheral fatigue) as a two-dimensional state, Amann & Dempsey (2008, PMID 17962334) show the defining signature of a real negative-feedback loop: two different pre-fatigue trajectories (67% vs 83% peak power) converge on the SAME end-exercise peripheral-fatigue ceiling (-35% to -37%, P=0.35, no difference) while central drive is suppressed in dose-dependent proportion to the pre-existing fatigue level. A passive, unregulated fatigability limit does not predict convergence from different starting trajectories -- a clamped feedback loop does. Cutting the loop (lumbar intrathecal fentanyl, blocking group III/IV afferent transmission) removes the clamp: the ceiling rises (to -44% to -52%) and central drive is measurably disinhibited (+9% to +21%), replicated in 3 independent trials, one (PMID 27241818) using a completely different observable (intramuscular metabolite chemistry from muscle biopsy) that itself correlates with the twitch-force deficit (r^2=0.79-0.92). This is a genuine, falsifiable regulator derived from a feedback loop's own defining signature (convergence-then-overshoot-when-cut), not a rhetorical label.

quadriceps_sustained_MVC_1min.pattern: 6/9 subjects show central fatigue (force falls faster than tetanic reference, EMG parallels force decline); 3/9 show little/no central fatigue (force parallels tetanic reference, EMG constant)

high_intensity_cycling_5km_TT_or_fixed_l.pattern: peripheral quadriceps-twitch decline converges to an invariant ~35-37% ceiling across different pre-fatigue trajectories when group III/IV afferents are intact; rises to 44-52% when blocked

prolonged_running_vs_cycling_vs_skiing.pattern: central fatigue after prolonged running measurable via multiple independent techniques; attenuated in lower-muscle-damage modalities (e.g. cycling) at matched duration; within running, magnitude of activation deficit scales with individual strength loss

submaximal_sustained_contractions_lt_15p.pattern: central fatigue demonstrable even here in brief nested maximal efforts; best submaximal signature is disproportionate rise in perceived effort, not VA decline directly

CFS.pattern: peripheral axis (metabolism, M-wave, twitch tension, systemic exercise response) statistically normal; central axis (VA during sustained maximal exercise) significantly reduced, 'well in excess of that found in controls'

MS.claim: Genuinely MIXED central + peripheral deficit -- forced, not oversold as purely central despite the more dramatic central number
MS.pattern: twitch-occlusion VA ceiling ~60% (vs ~100% normal) is the largest central deficit surveyed in this document; BUT an electrically-stimulated (voluntary-drive-bypassing) protocol independently shows excess tetanic-force/PCr/pH decline and delayed recovery in MS vs controls -- a real peripheral/excitation-contraction-coupling abnormality that survives with the central axis removed by construction

overtraining_syndrome.claim: Qualitatively coupled to chronic dysregulation of the same central-drive/afferent-feedback system, but NOT quantitatively established via twitch interpolation in this literature pass
overtraining_syndrome.honest_note: no validated marker of any kind exists per the field's own 2013 consensus statement; the located autonomic/HRR finding is directionally suggestive of altered central command in functional overreaching but is not a voluntary-activation measurement and should not be conflated with F1-F6's evidence chain

scoping_note_central_governor_model.not_certified_here: Noakes' broader 'Central Governor Model' (PMID 11581338, PMID 17465612, both title/journal/year/PMID confirmed live) extends to brain-mediated anticipatory pacing across all exercise performance -- a related but distinct, more theoretically expansive and more contested framework than the mechanistically-tested, pharmacologically-forced, decorrelated-leg-confirmed Amann group III/IV findings (F3) that this document actually certifies. Named explicitly to prevent the two from being conflated by a future reader or folding process.

All decisive Amann-lineage trials (F3) have small samples (n=7-8 per study) -- real, peer-reviewed, replicated across 3 independent papers from the same research group plus one decorrelated measurement axis, but not a large-cohort finding; the falsifier gate is set on direction+magnitude-across-replications rather than a single p-value for exactly this reason.

No twitch-interpolation number cited here was independently re-analyzed on raw trial-level data -- every value is the source paper's own reported abstract statistic (mean+/-SD or percentage), not recomputed from a downloaded dataset, consistent with this document's disclosed OPEN/HYPOTHESIS-B status.

Group III/IV muscle afferents (Amann's target -- metabo-/mechanoreceptive, working locomotor muscle) are anatomically and functionally distinct from the group III/IV JOINT afferents already cited in this repo's docs/MECHANISM_NOCICEPTION.md (posterior articular nerve, cat knee) -- same conduction-velocity-based numerical classification scheme, different receptive organ and reflex target; not conflated here.
proposed_cell: Extend scripts/msk/muscle_fatigue.py (the existing peripheral 3-compartment motor-unit fatigue/recovery ODE) with a CENTRAL-DRIVE multiplier CD(t) in (0,1] applied upstream of the existing TL(t) target-load input, parametrized by (1) a baseline-VA distribution drawn from the Allen/Gandevia/McKenzie (1995, PMID 7753121) reliability data (VA<100% in 75% of fresh contractions) and (2) a fatigue-dependent decay term calibrated to the Gandevia et al (1996, PMID 8821149) 3-minute-MVC trajectory (>99% to 90.7%). Decisive, cheap, fully machine-checkable test using data already on disk (zero new acquisition): does adding CD(t) change which muscle in this twin's own 80-muscle gait reconstruction is predicted to cross its own peak-demand/MF ceiling first (the mechanism MECHANISM_MUSCLE_FATIGUE.md sec.7 already derived from its own conservation law, MR+MA+MF=1)? A second, decisive follow-on: implement Amann's regulator explicitly as a closed-loop controller (peripheral-fatigue-state feeds back to suppress CD(t) target, replicating the invariant-ceiling signature from PMID 17962334) and test whether removing the feedback term (the in-silico equivalent of the fentanyl blockade) reproduces the same direction of ceiling-overshoot measured empirically (PMID 19015193/21878520/27241818).
